Subject: Re: Data residency & export controls — technical follow-up

Hi Susan — quick technical answers to the questions Marissa raised: 

1) EU region availability: We operate an EU-hosted region (region id: eu-west-1 for hosted API). For Hosted accounts you can pin a tenant to eu-west-1; we run inference in-region and do not replicate inference inputs/outputs out-of-region by default. For stronger guarantees (no egress path), Dedicated or Private deployments provide customer-managed networking and prevent cross-border flows.

2) Data residency guarantees: For Hosted pinned accounts we provide contractual commitments and config flags to limit replication. For Dedicated/Private you can ensure logs and KV cache are stored on customer-owned storage and KMS keys.

3) Key management & encryption: We support customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM integrations) for Dedicated and Private. For Hosted we offer envelope encryption and BYOK for enterprise plans.

4) SCCs & controller/processor: Redwood operates as a processor by default; we have standard SCCs we can include in the DPA. We can share the DPA excerpt that addresses cross-border transfers.

5) OFAC/ITAR & screening: We run sanctions screening for customer account onboarding and can restrict exports to sanctioned jurisdictions. For ITAR-specific use cases we recommend Private/on-prem deployments and a conversation with our legal team — happy to connect.

6) HIPAA / BAA: We support HIPAA workloads on Dedicated and Private deployments. For hosted customers we can discuss controls but the BAA path typically requires Dedicated/Private and a security review.

Attachments: redwood-eu-dataflow-diagram.png (diagram showing region flow and where KV cache lives).

If you want, I can join a technical call next week to walk through the network/data flow and show how we enforce in-region compute and KMS boundaries.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Staff Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
